newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index seen down on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index seen down on lack of demand.

text.p: A lack of investor demand dragged the Nairobi bourse index down on Monday, bourse officials and brokers said.
The index dropped 15.87 points to 3018.11. Turnover was 7.862 million shillings traded on 226,754 shares from 5.749 million shares traded on 146,730 shares on Friday.
"The market is depressed at the moment. There is no demand to support prices, which is why it is looking so unattractive at the moment," a senior broker said.
Kenya Airways eased to 9.00 from 9.35 while Diamond Trust Bank lost 75 cents to close at 33.50. Kenya Power & Lighting closed at 131 from 132 and oil concern Total Kenya lost 4.0 to close at 62.

A bourse official said investors appeared quite ready to dispose of their portions in shares such as Kenya Airways, Diamond Trust, Total Kenya and Kenya Power & Lighting Co at any price -- which brought down the share prices.

Foreign investors continued to dominate buying interest in Kenya Commercial Bank, Kenya Breweries and Firestone East Africa. They bought 52,900 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 56 and 57.50, 10,000 shares of Firestone East Africa at 24.25 and 12,600 shares at 50.

Financial analysts agreed that a number of shares in the market were undervalued. They said foreign investors were looking towards emerging markets to invest in what they thought were undervalued securities with strong potential for growth.
In the agriculturals, 7,500 shares of Rea Vipingo were traded at 10.55 from 10.35 while 100 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee were traded at 54 from 53.50.
